paragraphs.source_en: Nor was that all. On the twenty-first, Ieyasu passed through Sawayama, the former domain of Ishida Mitsunari, and when he reached Nagahara on the twenty-second, he received two separate reports: Shogun Hidetada had personally set out from Edo at the head of a great army, while Yoshinao, who had departed Nagoya in high spirits, had already reached Kyoto.

units.source_en: Nor was that all. On the twenty-first, Ieyasu passed through Sawayama, the former domain of Ishida Mitsunari, and when he reached Nagahara on the twenty-second, he received two separate reports: Shogun Hidetada had personally set out from Edo at the head of a great army, while Yoshinao, who had departed Nagoya in high spirits, had already reached Kyoto.

ja.t: それだけではなかった。

units.source_zh: 不止如此，家康二十一日经石田三成旧领地佐和山、二十二日抵永原时，分别接到了两个消息：一是将军秀忠已亲率大军从江户出发，另，意气风发从名古屋出发的义直，已抵京都。

paragraphs.source_zh: 不止如此，家康二十一日经石田三成旧领地佐和山、二十二日抵永原时，分别接到了两个消息：一是将军秀忠已亲率大军从江户出发，另，意气风发从名古屋出发的义直，已抵京都。

paragraphs.source_en: “Do not make undue haste, or the soldiers will easily become exhausted!” Ieyasu immediately sent a messenger to Hidetada.

units.source_en: “Do not make undue haste, or the soldiers will easily become exhausted!”
units.source_zh: “休要太急，否则士卒易疲惫！”

units.source_en: Ieyasu immediately sent a messenger to Hidetada.
units.source_zh: 家康立时向秀忠派去使者。

paragraphs.source_zh: “休要太急，否则士卒易疲惫！”家康立时向秀忠派去使者。

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu’s advance was neither hurried nor slow, but it was by no means at a standstill. As the distance to Osaka dwindled, he placed his pieces one by one, so that all the world might see the unmistakable difference between a grown man and a child.

units.source_en: Ieyasu’s advance was neither hurried nor slow, but it was by no means at a standstill.

ja.t: みしていたわけではない。

units.source_zh: 家康的进军不急不缓，但决非停滞不前。

units.source_en: As the distance to Osaka dwindled, he placed his pieces one by one, so that all the world might see the unmistakable difference between a grown man and a child.
units.source_zh: 随着与大坂间距离的缩短，他一步步下出棋子，好令世人看出成人和小儿之间明显的差距。

paragraphs.source_zh: 家康的进军不急不缓，但决非停滞不前。随着与大坂间距离的缩短，他一步步下出棋子，好令世人看出成人和小儿之间明显的差距。

paragraphs.source_en: Shogun Hidetada remained measured and composed, which afforded Ieyasu some reassurance. To Hidetada, however, such restraint seemed irresponsible and lacking in filial devotion. Before receiving Ieyasu’s permission to take the field, Hidetada told Tōdō Takatora, “The Ōgosho’s orders have not yet arrived, but I have decided to march.” He intended to act first and report afterward.

units.source_en: Shogun Hidetada remained measured and composed, which afforded Ieyasu some reassurance.
units.source_zh: 将军秀忠尚不温不火，还算令家康安心。

units.source_en: To Hidetada, however, such restraint seemed irresponsible and lacking in filial devotion.

ja.t: にしてみれば、そのように

units.source_zh: 但在秀忠看来，这却是不负责任和孝心不足。

units.source_en: Before receiving Ieyasu’s permission to take the field, Hidetada told Tōdō Takatora, “The Ōgosho’s orders have not yet arrived, but I have decided to march.”
units.source_zh: 在未得到家康允许出兵之前，秀忠对藤堂高虎道：“大御所的指令虽还没到，但我已决定出兵。”

units.source_en: He intended to act first and report afterward.

ja.t: るつもりだったのである。

units.source_zh: 他欲先斩后奏。

paragraphs.source_zh: 将军秀忠尚不温不火，还算令家康安心。但在秀忠看来，这却是不负责任和孝心不足。在未得到家康允许出兵之前，秀忠对藤堂高虎道：“大御所的指令虽还没到，但我已决定出兵。”他欲先斩后奏。

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu advancing in a palanquin and Hidetada marching at the head of a great army—one slow, the other swift—left the world with utterly different impressions. The former suggested that Osaka still had room to “change its mind”; the latter, by contrast, showed no such consideration.

units.source_en: Ieyasu advancing in a palanquin and Hidetada marching at the head of a great army—one slow, the other swift—left the world with utterly different impressions.
units.source_zh: 家康乘坐轿舆进军和秀忠率领大军进发，一缓一急，给世人留下了截然不同的印象。

units.source_en: The former suggested that Osaka still had room to “change its mind”; the latter, by contrast, showed no such consideration.
units.source_zh: 前者令人感觉大坂尚有“反悔”余地，与此相反，后者则毫无顾忌。

paragraphs.source_zh: 家康乘坐轿舆进军和秀忠率领大军进发，一缓一急，给世人留下了截然不同的印象。前者令人感觉大坂尚有“反悔”余地，与此相反，后者则毫无顾忌。

paragraphs.source_en: Upon learning that Hidetada had taken the field, Takenaka Shigetoshi, now lord of Funai Castle in Bungo, personally sent a messenger to Tadakatsu, son of Fukushima Masanori, lord of Hiroshima Castle in Aki. Masanori was in Edo, but unless Tadakatsu immediately led his troops to join the army attacking Osaka, he might incur Hidetada’s suspicion; Shigetoshi’s message was therefore a deliberate admonition.

units.source_en: Upon learning that Hidetada had taken the field, Takenaka Shigetoshi, now lord of Funai Castle in Bungo, personally sent a messenger to Tadakatsu, son of Fukushima Masanori, lord of Hiroshima Castle in Aki.
units.source_zh: 已是丰后府内城主的竹中重利得知秀忠出兵，便亲自向安艺广岛城主福岛正则之子忠胜派出使者。

units.source_en: Masanori was in Edo, but unless Tadakatsu immediately led his troops to join the army attacking Osaka, he might incur Hidetada’s suspicion; Shigetoshi’s message was therefore a deliberate admonition.
units.source_zh: 正则人在江户，但忠胜若不立刻率兵加入进攻大坂之军，恐受到秀忠怀疑，故，重利此行乃是刻意进言。

paragraphs.source_zh: 已是丰后府内城主的竹中重利得知秀忠出兵，便亲自向安艺广岛城主福岛正则之子忠胜派出使者。正则人在江户，但忠胜若不立刻率兵加入进攻大坂之军，恐受到秀忠怀疑，故，重利此行乃是刻意进言。

paragraphs.source_en: At that moment, news arrived that displeased Ieyasu still further. Acting under Ieyasu’s orders, Tōdō Takatora, commander of the vanguard, instructed Katagiri Katsumoto and his son Takatoshi to lead the attack on Osaka. The Katagiris immediately surrendered their hostages and gladly accepted.

units.source_en: At that moment, news arrived that displeased Ieyasu still further.
units.source_zh: 此时，一则令家康更为不快的消息送了来。

units.source_en: Acting under Ieyasu’s orders, Tōdō Takatora, commander of the vanguard, instructed Katagiri Katsumoto and his son Takatoshi to lead the attack on Osaka. The Katagiris immediately surrendered their hostages and gladly accepted.
units.source_zh: 担任先锋的藤堂高虎受家康之命，令片桐且元与其子孝利担任攻打大坂的前锋，片桐父子立刻交出人质，欣然从命。

paragraphs.source_zh: 此时，一则令家康更为不快的消息送了来。担任先锋的藤堂高虎受家康之命，令片桐且元与其子孝利担任攻打大坂的前锋，片桐父子立刻交出人质，欣然从命。

paragraphs.source_en: Tōdō Takatora had divined Ieyasu’s intentions in assigning Katagiri Katsumoto to the vanguard: naturally, the appointment was also meant to let him communicate with the peace faction inside the castle. Yet the Katagiris unexpectedly accepted at once—how pitiable Hideyori’s position had become! Those who ought to have become Osaka’s allies departed one after another, while unexpected people brought Ieyasu information damaging to Osaka and turned their hearts toward the eastern government.

units.source_en: Tōdō Takatora had divined Ieyasu’s intentions in assigning Katagiri Katsumoto to the vanguard: naturally, the appointment was also meant to let him communicate with the peace faction inside the castle.
units.source_zh: 藤堂高虎揣摩着家康的心思，让片桐且元担任先锋，这里面当然含有让他和城内主和众人联络的意思。

units.source_en: Yet the Katagiris unexpectedly accepted at once—how pitiable Hideyori’s position had become!
units.source_zh: 不意片桐父子立刻就答应下来，可见秀赖何等可悲！

units.source_en: Those who ought to have become Osaka’s allies departed one after another, while unexpected people brought Ieyasu information damaging to Osaka and turned their hearts toward the eastern government.
units.source_zh: 本应成为大坂盟友的人陆续离去，意想不到的人皆把不利于大坂的消息带给家康，心向关东。

paragraphs.source_zh: 藤堂高虎揣摩着家康的心思，让片桐且元担任先锋，这里面当然含有让他和城内主和众人联络的意思。不意片桐父子立刻就答应下来，可见秀赖何等可悲！本应成为大坂盟友的人陆续离去，意想不到的人皆把不利于大坂的消息带给家康，心向关东。

paragraphs.source_en: Hidetada’s advance made a negotiated peace more impossible still.

units.source_en: Hidetada’s advance made a negotiated peace more impossible still.
units.source_zh: 秀忠的进兵，更是令讲和变得不能。

paragraphs.source_zh: 秀忠的进兵，更是令讲和变得不能。

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu could no longer halt his steps. On the twenty-third of the tenth month, he proceeded directly into Nijō Castle in Kyoto.

units.source_en: Ieyasu could no longer halt his steps.

ja.t: めることができなかった。

units.source_zh: 家康已无法停下脚步。

units.source_en: On the twenty-third of the tenth month, he proceeded directly into Nijō Castle in Kyoto.
units.source_zh: 十月二十三，他径直进驻京都二条城。

paragraphs.source_zh: 家康已无法停下脚步。十月二十三，他径直进驻京都二条城。

paragraphs.source_en: After entering Nijō Castle, Ieyasu once again sent a messenger to Hidetada, who was advancing westward along the Tōkaidō: “Do not be impatient. The art of war teaches that a long march against a distant objective bears the signs of defeat. You must show concern for the soldiers’ hardships and advance with stately dignity.”

units.source_en: After entering Nijō Castle, Ieyasu once again sent a messenger to Hidetada, who was advancing westward along the Tōkaidō: “Do not be impatient.
units.source_zh: 进入二条城，家康再次向沿东海道西上的秀忠派出了使者：“不可着急。

units.source_en: The art of war teaches that a long march against a distant objective bears the signs of defeat.
units.source_zh: 兵法云：长途袭远，败军之象。

units.source_en: You must show concern for the soldiers’ hardships and advance with stately dignity.”
units.source_zh: 必体恤士卒的疾苦，威风凛凛进兵为宜。”

paragraphs.source_zh: 进入二条城，家康再次向沿东海道西上的秀忠派出了使者：“不可着急。兵法云：长途袭远，败军之象。必体恤士卒的疾苦，威风凛凛进兵为宜。”

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu was employing the strategy of “intimidation” so often used by the late Taikō. For the moment, Ieyasu hoped by this means to induce Hideyori to reflect upon his course. And not Hideyori alone: he also wanted the rōnin who had flocked to Osaka Castle in hopes of throwing the realm into turmoil to recognize the prevailing course of the age, change their minds, and abandon resistance.

units.source_en: Ieyasu was employing the strategy of “intimidation” so often used by the late Taikō.
units.source_zh: 家康所施，为已故太阁常用的“威压”之略。

units.source_en: For the moment, Ieyasu hoped by this means to induce Hideyori to reflect upon his course.
units.source_zh: 家康目下乃是想借此促使秀赖反省。

units.source_en: And not Hideyori alone: he also wanted the rōnin who had flocked to Osaka Castle in hopes of throwing the realm into turmoil to recognize the prevailing course of the age, change their minds, and abandon resistance.
units.source_zh: 不只是秀赖，他还欲令唯恐天下不乱而聚到大坂城的浪人，看清天下大势，好让他们改变初衷，放弃对抗。

paragraphs.source_zh: 家康所施，为已故太阁常用的“威压”之略。家康目下乃是想借此促使秀赖反省。不只是秀赖，他还欲令唯恐天下不乱而聚到大坂城的浪人，看清天下大势，好让他们改变初衷，放弃对抗。

paragraphs.source_en: But circumstances had already changed. Had these men been Takeda Shingen, Hōjō Ujimasa, Kobayakawa Takakage, or Uesugi Kenshin, the moment the disparity in military strength was displayed to them, they would never have entertained thoughts of battle again, whatever they might have felt inwardly. But these children of the present knew nothing of the battlefield, nor did they understand the terror of war or the disparity in strength.

units.source_en: But circumstances had already changed.
units.source_zh: 可情势已然发生变换。

units.source_en: Had these men been Takeda Shingen, Hōjō Ujimasa, Kobayakawa Takakage, or Uesugi Kenshin, the moment the disparity in military strength was displayed to them, they would never have entertained thoughts of battle again, whatever they might have felt inwardly.

ja.t: こすことはなかったはずである。

units.source_zh: 若是武田信玄、北条氏政、小早川隆景、上杉谦信诸人，一旦向他们显示出兵力差别，不论他们内心怎样，必不会再生战意。

units.source_en: But these children of the present knew nothing of the battlefield, nor did they understand the terror of war or the disparity in strength.
units.source_zh: 但目下这些小儿从不知战阵为何物，亦不明战事的可怕和实力的差距。

paragraphs.source_zh: 可情势已然发生变换。若是武田信玄、北条氏政、小早川隆景、上杉谦信诸人，一旦向他们显示出兵力差别，不论他们内心怎样，必不会再生战意。但目下这些小儿从不知战阵为何物，亦不明战事的可怕和实力的差距。

paragraphs.source_en: The daimyō of the realm who streamed into Nijō Castle were all convinced that Ieyasu was enraged and resolved to subjugate Osaka, and each clamored for the honor of leading the attack.

units.source_en: The daimyō of the realm who streamed into Nijō Castle were all convinced that Ieyasu was enraged and resolved to subjugate Osaka, and each clamored for the honor of leading the attack.
units.source_zh: 接连聚往二条城的天下大名，都坚信家康很是愤怒，决意要讨伐大坂，遂纷纷请求打头阵。

paragraphs.source_zh: 接连聚往二条城的天下大名，都坚信家康很是愤怒，决意要讨伐大坂，遂纷纷请求打头阵。

paragraphs.source_en: First Katagiri Katsumoto and his son Takatoshi came forward to volunteer, followed by Hosokawa Tadaoki. Each of them disclosed Osaka’s internal affairs to Ieyasu. In truth, however, Ieyasu already knew the situation inside the castle in every detail, and that knowledge filled him with sorrow.

units.source_en: First Katagiri Katsumoto and his son Takatoshi came forward to volunteer, followed by Hosokawa Tadaoki.
units.source_zh: 首先是片桐且元与其子孝利前来请命，接着为细川忠兴。

units.source_en: Each of them disclosed Osaka’s internal affairs to Ieyasu.
units.source_zh: 每人都向家康透露了大坂内情。

units.source_en: In truth, however, Ieyasu already knew the situation inside the castle in every detail, and that knowledge filled him with sorrow.
units.source_zh: 但实际上，家康对城内情形一清二楚，为此大为悲哀。

paragraphs.source_zh: 首先是片桐且元与其子孝利前来请命，接着为细川忠兴。每人都向家康透露了大坂内情。但实际上，家康对城内情形一清二楚，为此大为悲哀。

paragraphs.source_en: That day, Ieyasu lent two hundred kan of silver apiece to Asano Nagaakira—who had contributed funds to the restoration of Edo Castle and had now also dispatched troops—and to Nabeshima Katsushige, Yamauchi Tadayoshi, and others. He then ordered Hosokawa Tadaoki and the rest to advance east together as soon as the forces of Mōri Terumoto and Shimazu Iehisa set out.

units.source_en: That day, Ieyasu lent two hundred kan of silver apiece to Asano Nagaakira—who had contributed funds to the restoration of Edo Castle and had now also dispatched troops—and to Nabeshima Katsushige, Yamauchi Tadayoshi, and others. He then ordered Hosokawa Tadaoki and the rest to advance east together as soon as the forces of Mōri Terumoto and Shimazu Iehisa set out.
units.source_zh: 是日，家康分别借与为江户城的修复出钱、此次又出兵的浅野长晟，及锅岛胜茂、山内忠义等人银二百贯，命细川忠兴等人待毛利辉元与岛津家久的人马甫一出发，一起东进。

paragraphs.source_zh: 是日，家康分别借与为江户城的修复出钱、此次又出兵的浅野长晟，及锅岛胜茂、山内忠义等人银二百贯，命细川忠兴等人待毛利辉元与岛津家久的人马甫一出发，一起东进。

paragraphs.source_en: By now, it had become a sorrowful grand military exercise engulfing the entire realm.

units.source_en: By now, it had become a sorrowful grand military exercise engulfing the entire realm.
units.source_zh: 至此，这俨然是一场席卷天下的可悲大演兵。

paragraphs.source_zh: 至此，这俨然是一场席卷天下的可悲大演兵。
